content: AT-SPI automation pitfalls: Chromium builds the accessibility tree only when an AT connects or when launched with ACCESSIBILITY_ENABLED=1 plus --force-renderer-accessibility (SO 26152972; flag has had version regressions, e.g. Chrome 117 thread). Tree is built asynchronously - automation must poll/wait after launch and after focus changes. GNOME is redesigning the protocol (at-spi2-core new-protocol doc: per-surface trees vs tree-per-application). E2e stand must activate target windows itself (spec 7.3) and tolerate stale/focus-less trees; gnome-text-editor/gedit expose AtkText, Chromium needs the flags.
